full_judgment:
12. Now let me analyses the findings arrived at by the court of appeal below and see whether that can be sustained in law. The finding of the trial court that the plaintiff has been able to prove his case has been reversal by the appellate court below on the ground that the trial court without properly considering the documentary evidence arrived at such a wrong and erroneous finding because according to the lower appellate court Exhibit D and Dl show that the plaintiff is a co-sharer with the defendants in the suit plot. I along with the learned Advocates of both the sides meticulously examined the case record. 

 21. Mr. Saha while arguing in support of the rule submitted that the judgment of the lower appellate court cannot be termed as a proper judgment of reversal at all because it has utterly failed to comply with the requirement of Order 41 Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure and for this purpose he has relied on the case reported in 14 B.L.D. (AD) 229 wherein it has been held that the appellate court whether reversing or affirming the decision of the trial Court must independently discuss and consider the evidence on record. But in the case of affirming the finding of the trial court, the narration of the entire evidence and reiteration of the reasons are not essential. In such a case expressions of general agreement with those of the trial Court are generally considered sufficient. But in the case of a reversal of a judgment, the consideration of the evidence, of necessity, has to be thorough and more elaborate.
